messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high error rate observed for model-serving runtime group 'infer-prod-usw2'. Symptoms: 5xx spike (~18% 5xx), timeouts, some segfaults logged on runner pods. Pager routed to @Dave (oncall) at 17:02 UTC.
Dave (oncall): I'm on it. any customer reports yet?
Eli (support): Got a ticket from AcmeCorp reporting timeouts on API calls ~17:00 UTC, they see 502s.
Alice: I'm seeing a huge tail in runtime logs: repeated oom-kill and a few ``SIGSEGV`` from model-runner-3. Pod restarts correlate with the 5xx spike.
Ben: Check node metrics — GPU memory pressure on a subset of hosts (gpu-node-17..19). Might be a quantized model path causing runaway allocation after token growth.
Dave (oncall): Okay, immediate plan: 1) divert new traffic from infer-prod-usw2 to infer-prod-use1 fallback pool, 2) scale up dedicated fallback nodes, 3) collect core dumps from crashing pods.
Cara: I'm toggling routing policy to prefer region fallback now (`/runbook route set-policy infer-prod us-west2 -> use1 priority=1`). Will also enable model-variant fallback to smaller-quant model.
ops-bot: Executed: `route-policy update infer-prod us-west-2 -> us-east-1` by Cara at 17:07 UTC. :white_check_mark:
Dave (oncall): Starting a controlled restart of model-runner pods on affected nodes (sequential) to avoid thundering herd. Also adding `--enable-kernel-fallback` to the runtime flags on affected ASG.
Alice: Pasting recent runner log snippet (from model-runner-3):
```
[17:00:12] ERROR inference/runtime.cc:423 - allocation failed: requested 1.2GB but only 128MB free
[17:00:12] WARNING kernel: falling back to slow-path kernel
[17:00:15] INFO model_runner: flushing kv cache
[17:00:16] FATAL signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f8a3c12
backtrace:
  runner+0x1f3a
  libtorch.so+0x45cde
  ...
```
Alice: There are multiple `allocation failed` lines before the segfaults. Looks like a memory growth pattern then crash.
Ben: I'm attaching a quick kdump collection command to pull cores: `kubectl exec -n infer -it model-runner-3 -- tar -cz /var/crash /var/log/model-runner > /tmp/model-runner-3-crash.tgz` — start that on other crashy pods too.
Cara: Traffic shift + smaller model variant seems to have reduced error rate to ~6% within 5 minutes. Keep monitoring.
Eli (support): Notifying AcmeCorp that we've detected a runtime incident and are routing them to fallback while we investigate. They reported degraded throughput only, no data leak.
Dave (oncall): I'm going to cordon gpu-node-18 to prevent new pods landing while we debug. Setting host-level guard.
ops-bot: Node cordon executed for gpu-node-18 by Dave at 17:12 UTC.
Alice: Dumped KV-cache sizes for the hot runners — one session shows KV growth to 14GB after long prefix expansions (long chat-history prompts). That plus a quantization edge-case is likely overflowing the allocator.
Ben: Suggest immediate mitigation: enable prefix-KV eviction/limit in runtime config for host pool `infer-prod-usw2` to 1GB per session. Also disable the quant-attn optimized kernel until we have a repro.
Dave (oncall): Applying eviction limit now (`redwoodctl runtime set --pool infer-prod-usw2 --kv-max-per-session 1GB`).
Cara: Rolling restart of the runtime on the affected ASG with `--disable-quant-attn` to avoid the kernel path. Doing that in canary first (gpu-node-17).
Dave (oncall): Also toggled canary=on then off to ensure old traffic drains: `infra deploy canary infer-runtime v2026.03.1 --disable-quant-attn`.
Alice: Core dumps uploaded to /mnt/ingest/crashdumps/1767009999/ — one core shows crash in quantized attention path. I'll open a debug ticket with stack and bin exact hashes.
Eli (support): Customer update sent: "We've routed your traffic to a fallback region and are applying runtime mitigations. No user data at risk. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause"
Cara: Observability: added temporary dashboards to track per-pool 5xx, per-node GPU mem used, kv-cache bytes per session.
ops-bot: Observability alerts adjusted: firing threshold now 5% 5xx for infer-prod pools at 5m.
Dave (oncall): Error rate now 1.2% after fallback and eviction. Latency stable. Any outstanding tasks?
Alice: Need a follow-up: reproduce locally with long prefix to verify kv-growth bug and create a regression test. Also create a canary rollout plan to re-enable quant-attn after patch.
Ben: I'll create a CR to back out quant-attn from the kernel selector and instrument better OOM checks in allocator.
Cara: I'll coordinate customer-facing postmortem and advise on recommended client-side limits to prevent extremely long context sessions for now.
Eli (support): Marking affected customers list and outreach status in the incident doc.
Dave (oncall): Handing off to Alice (day shift) for post-incident follow-up. Handoff notes: core dumps collected, routing rollback in monitor ready, blocked quant-attn kernel, follow-up RC: 1767012000.
Alice: Acknowledged. Will take on RCA and the follow-ups.
ops-bot: Incident ticket updated: severity=high, status=mitigated, assigned_to=Alice, followup=memory-growth-repro+kernel-fix.
Cara: Quick summary for the log: root cause likely kv-cache growth combined with quantized attention kernel edge-case causing allocator exhaustion -> segfaults -> 5xx cascade. Mitigations: routing fallback, kv eviction limit, disable quant-attn kernel, node cordon/restarts.
Dave (oncall): Great work team. :thumbsup: I'll remove the pager duty escalation.
Eli (support): I'll send closure notes to customers once postmortem is ready.
Alice: Adding action items: reproducer, kernel fix, add runtime guardrails (kv-limits + early OOM backpressure), test coverage, customer comms.
Cara: Will draft postmortem and timeline. ETA 48h.
ops-bot: Thread closed by Dave at 18:40 UTC."
